Chapter 12. Rethinking the Human Place: Lessons from Animal Minds.
You know, the more we discover about animal intelligence, the more those old ideas about humans being at the very top start to crumble. That image of a ladder—with us on the highest rung and all the other creatures below—just doesn't hold up anymore.
Instead, imagine a branching tree. Every species has its own unique path, shaped by what it needs to survive and the challenges it faces. It’s not about one being better than another—it’s about different ways of thinking, feeling, and making sense of the world.
And this change isn’t just about science. It’s personal, too. It shifts how we see ourselves, and how we connect with the world around us. Suddenly, the line between “us” and “them” gets a little blurry—a bit softer, a bit more open.
So, the real question isn’t, “Are we smart enough to figure out how smart animals are?” Instead, it’s, “Are we wise enough to notice all the intelligence that surrounds us every day?”
Our world is so much richer, more complex, and more beautiful than we ever imagined. And in this world, every creature—big or small—has its own story to tell.
